⭕️ Resistance, perseverance, and four-dimensional care

To protect Iran against colonial and multi-stage weakening schemes (especially until a new equilibrium is achieved in the region), we need the following simultaneously and in synergy:

1️⃣ Military resistance
2️⃣ Diplomatic resistance
3️⃣ Social perseverance, and
4️⃣ Economic care for the most disadvantaged citizens

Any force that pays insufficient attention to any one of these four dimensions of national resistance and perseverance, and fails to accept what is required to strengthen them all at once, will inadvertently diminish our national endurance and capacity to make it through the formidable passes that lie ahead.

@jalaeipour

The second episode of the Neshan podcast, titled "On the Shores of the Red Sea," has been released. In this episode, we hear how Yemen's fate became intertwined with the decision of the King of Iran. Before the rise of Islam, Yemen had become an arena of rivalry between Iran, Rome, and Abyssinia—a rivalry that was not only about power but also centered on the trade routes of the Red Sea. Amid these conflicts, one of Yemen's notables traveled to the court of Khosrow Anushirvan to seek Iran's help in expelling the Abyssinian rulers. In the second episode of the "Neshan" podcast, we learn the story of a small army from Iran that marched on Yemen—an event that led to the formation of the Iranian community in Yemen and left traces that endured into the early years of Islam. You can now listen to this episode on Castbox and Shenoto. entry.title: [jalaeipour] Being Iranian is a blend of wisdom, justice, liberty, and love—four pillars…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @jalaeipour

Being Iranian is a blend of wisdom, justice, liberty, and love—four pillars on which our culture rests. A culture's pillars should not be judged merely by how faithfully people adhere to them today; we must also ask what values a culture possesses that enable it to recognize and correct its own shortcomings. These four pillars are not a claim that Iranians are flawless; they are an ethical and cultural horizon we can lean on to build a better society. Wisdom, justice, liberty, and love are neither imported values nor newly invented ideals; they are rooted in our own history and intellectual and cultural heritage. From the Avesta and the teachings of truth and asha, to the admonition books of ancient Iran and their emphasis on wisdom and justice; from Ferdowsi's Shahnameh and its praise of wisdom, justice, and liberty, to the works of Saadi and other great figures of Persian literature who have honored love and humanism—the continuity of these values is visible. These four pillars are not meant to describe the behavior of all Iranians in all eras. They are criteria rooted in our culture, and we can even draw on them to critique the shortcomings of today's society. If there is foolishness, wisdom remains a virtue; if there is injustice, justice remains a value; if there is baseness and flattery, liberty remains an ideal; and if there is violence and hatred, love remains an ethical necessity.
